seen.outcome: REBUILT 2026-08-05 from the recorded design constraint. TWO independent checkers, one fix cycle, targeted re-check FAILED. Not staged. Branch ship/003-codeowners pushed, unmerged, ledger status failed. Re-enters as a REBUILD with a TWO-LINE constraint - the cheapest pick available.
seen.note: The rebuild did what the constraint asked and it worked: lib/door.js validates every dimension at the door with zero allocation (rejects the 23,701 ms input in 0.007 ms), output is bounded by construction (largest measured #result.innerHTML 994,680 of a 1,000,000 bound, well-formed, disclosure always present), paint is measured across two animation frames and printed under every answer, and the prose is a range over 24 repeated trials instead of a single reading. Round 1 found five defects; one fix cycle cured four of them under adversarial re-test. Round 2 failed it on TWO NEW defects the fix itself introduced or exposed. Inherited proven and NOT to be re-derived: 171/171 reference pairs, 13/13 GitHub-documented, 6/6 line-skipping, all against the LIVE page in both rounds; ~55-66 XSS positions, 0 injections, 0 dialogs; build byte-reproducible; 0 cookies/storage, 2 requests; mobile 375px clean.
seen.rebuild_constraint: TWO changes, both design, neither a patch. (1) THE DOOR NEEDS TWO LINE CAPS, NOT ONE. Non-blank lines bound DOWNSTREAM WORK; TOTAL SEGMENTS bound the PREPROCESSING between the door and the budget. Counting only non-blank lines fixed the trailing-newline off-by-one and simultaneously let ~1,000,000 blank segments through into an unmetered split() + per-line trim, measured by the re-checker at 1,309-1,342 ms reported and 16-34 s wall clock on a fully door-legal input. Binding rule: the door must bound EVERY quantity that ANY loop between the door and the budget will iterate over, and no raw split may be taken over a quantity the door has not bounded. Add maxSegments alongside maxLines in lib/door.js and assert both at the page. (2) REPLACE THE RE-ENTRANCY BOOLEAN WITH A GENERATION COUNTER. `running` is a lock with no release path on the re-entrant case: an input arriving while a prior run's post-paint measurement is pending is dropped, and the page can strand permanently on 'working...' while data-state reads idle - reproduced deterministically and stable for 10+ s with no self-correction. A monotonic generation, where a stale generation's completion is discarded and the newest input always schedules a run, cannot deadlock and cannot drop the latest answer. (3) Then re-derive the printed timing range from measurement again, because (1) changes the worst case. (4) Start from lib/checks/door-limits.json + lib/checks/codeowners-oracle.json - both already carry the probes and the regression notes.

seen.note: XSS fixed and confirmed dead; 56/56 vs GitHub cheat sheet, 0 inverted verdicts. Fails on a glob-engine ReDoS that a static complexity budget cannot bound. REVISIT AS A REBUILD, not a new candidate: replace globToRegex/gmatch with a linear-time non-backtracking matcher (two-pointer + backtrack memo, or DP), verify against the existing 56-case published oracle and the ~67M-pair differential harness.
seen.rebuild_constraint: Replace globToRegex/gmatch with a LINEAR-TIME non-backtracking matcher (two-pointer with backtrack memo, or DP over pattern x path). BORROW: port nektos/act pkg/workflowpattern (MIT, correct GitHub semantics, scores 49/49) rather than hand-roll — hand-rolling is what produced the XSS then the ReDoS. VERIFY against lib/checks/gha-filter-oracle.json (46 published pairs) + lib/checks/redos-probes.json (must resolve <50ms each, no UI freeze) + lib/checks/xss-payloads.json. Add the LIVE analytics beacon (ship 002 predates it). Kill-criterion in per-path visits, not tool-runs. [2026-08-03 CORRECTION, from reading the port source rather than trusting the plan: act is linear-time because Go's regexp is RE2, NOT because of its pattern translation. PatternToRegex emits ordinary regex text. A VERBATIM JS PORT WOULD REINTRODUCE THE ReDoS, because JS RegExp backtracks. Port act's SEMANTICS line-for-line; execute them on a Thompson NFA / Pike-VM state-set simulation, never on JS RegExp.]
